title.narrative: EMERGECNY CASH-BASED ASSISTANCE FOR VULNERABLE PASTORALIST HOUSEHOLDS IN ZEYLAC DISTRICT, AWDAL REGION, SOMALILAND PROJECT.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe persistent dry conditions that had been forecast to last until June in Somalia have continued through September and October in the North with varying impacts. FAO/SWALIM indicates that an estimated 2.5 million people across 26 districts in Puntland and Somaliland have been moderately or severely impacted. By August, a total of 887,000 people were residing in areas classified as severely affected by drought across 16 districts, based on the relatively higher proportion of their populations living in the severely affected zones. An additional 1.6 million people were living in moderately affected areas, spanning 26 districts. The most recent Climate Update from SWALIM climate update released on 14 October pointed to below-normal rainfall and above-normal temperatures across most of Somalia with continuing dry conditions in northern regions.ltbrgt In response to the drought, both the Puntland and Somaliland authorities have already begun response activities with support from humanitarian partners. These efforts however fall far short of satisfactorily addressing the most critical needs in food security, nutrition, health and water and sanitation among the worst affected communities. The gravity of the funding cuts has also stretched available resources across Somalia as demonstrated by reports of the closure of crucial health and nutrition facilities and programmes, cuts in food assistance allocations and reduced human resource capacity.ltbrgtZeylac District, located in the westernmost part of the Awdal Region of Somaliland, is home to predominantly pastoralist communities whose livelihoods depend heavily on livestock production and seasonal rainfall. In recent years, the region has experienced increasingly erratic weather patterns, culminating in a prolonged and severe drought that has devastated local ecosystems and household economies.ltbrgtAccording to recent humanitarian assessments, Awdal Region is among the areas most severely affected by drought in northern Somalia, with Zeylac and neighboring Lughaya districts facing acute water shortages, pasture depletion, and widespread livestock mortality. The Somaliland government, National Disaster Food Reserve Agency (NADFOR) and the Humanitarian agencies have flagged the situation as critical, prompting urgent calls for humanitarian intervention.ltbrgtThe drought has led to:ltbrgt Significant loss of livestock, particularly among smallholder pastoralistsltbrgt Sharp declines in household income and food accessltbrgt Increased displacement, as families migrate in search of water and pastureltbrgt Rising malnutrition rates, especially among children and pregnant womenltbrgtTraditional coping mechanisms—such as selling livestock, borrowing food, or migrating—have been exhausted, leaving many households on the brink of destitution. ltbrgtTo address these urgent needs, this project proposes a three-month emergency cash-based response that combines:ltbrgt Unconditional cash transfers (UCT) to meet immediate food needsltbrgt Cash Plus support (UCT + emergency livestock inputs) to sustain animal health lp ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe targeting process combines community-based nomination and vulnerability scoring to ensure transparent, inclusive, and SHF/FSC compliant beneficiary selection. In Zeylac District, Village Relief Committees (VRCs) identified households most affected by drought and displacement, while project staff validated these lists using objective vulnerability criteria. The majority of targeted households are drought affected pastoralists who have lost significant livestock assets, with high dependency ratios and limited coping capacity. Approximately one quarter of beneficiaries are IDPs or returnees, reflecting displacement dynamics in the district. Women, elderly, persons with disabilities, and minority clans are prioritized to prevent exclusion and strengthen protection mainstreaming. This hybrid approach ensures that assistance reaches households most at risk of food insecurity while reinforcing community ownership, accountability, and donor compliance.ltbrgtlt/pgt
